assessment.nobel_worthiness: Localising gamma-ray bursts with X-ray afterglows, then optical and radio counterparts and redshifts, settled the distance scale of GRBs and turned them into cosmological probes and a window onto stellar collapse and black-hole formation. It is a discovery enabled by an instrument, BeppoSAX with its wide-field cameras and narrow-field telescopes, which is the kind of work I value most as a detector builder.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX X-ray localisation and the first afterglow detection in 1997; Kulkarni's group secured the early optical, radio and redshift follow-up that fixed the cosmological origin. The three form a coherent triad. Other important contributors (for example the optical identification teams and those who are deceased) cannot be credited from this list, so the split between X-ray and ground-based follow-up is not entirely clean.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades of confirmation by Swift, Fermi and ground facilities; the cosmological origin is firmly established and the field has matured, so recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation between the satellite team and the follow-up teams is debatable and a posthumous contributor cannot be recognised.
My judgement of who was decisive in the optical identification relies on recollection, not independently verified sources.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and later associating neutrinos with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened neutrino astronomy. IceCube, a cubic kilometre of instrumented Antarctic ice, is a remarkable detector achievement and squarely within my field of astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA and is the single credited name. Realising the instrument was a very large collaborative effort, and a single-laureate prize would understate that, but only the supplied credited name can be proposed.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is independently seen in several channels; source identification is still partial, with only a few individual sources at modest significance. Timing is reasonable but the scientific payoff is still growing.
uncertainties: The list supports only one name, so the prize configuration is narrow relative to the collaborative nature of the work.
Source associations such as TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 are statistically modest and not yet independently confirmed by other detectors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks at the magic wavelength reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. It is a precision-measurement instrument advance with clear lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and first demonstrated it with strontium; Ye's group drove the stability and accuracy records. The two-person credit is clean. Whether Hall and Hänsch (2005) comb recognition leaves room is a matter for colleagues; I defer to experts in atomic physics.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many laboratories with multiple species; the technology is mature and the redefinition of the second is being prepared, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Ion-clock and Al+ contributions (e.g. by others not credited here) may be viewed as comparably decisive.
I am not an atomic-physics specialist and rely on colleagues for the relative merit against other AMO candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC by ATLAS and CMS was a landmark in particle physics, achieved with detector systems of extraordinary scale and precision. The theoretical prediction was recognised in 2013, so the question is whether the experimental achievement merits a separate award.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee conceived and led the ATLAS and CMS projects over decades; they are credible leaders of the detector programmes. Whether leadership of collaborations of thousands is the decisive contribution compared with specific physics analyses or accelerator builders is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Discovery confirmed independently by two experiments and thoroughly characterised; recognition is mature, perhaps late, though the Nobel statute and the 2013 award complicate it.
uncertainties: The 2013 prize for the theory reduces the appetite for a second Higgs-related award.
Credit within huge collaborations and between detector founders and analysis leaders remains disputed.
Prize statutes limit the number of laureates, so omitting accelerator and trigger contributors is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic oscillation feature is a standard ruler imprinted in galaxy clustering, giving robust distance measurements that underpin dark-energy constraints. It combines a clean physical idea with large survey instruments.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein's SDSS luminous-red-galaxy detection and Cole and Percival's 2dFGRS analysis in 2005 were the first detections. The credited names represent the two surveys fairly, though the theoretical prediction of the feature by earlier authors (for example Peebles and Yu, Sunyaev and Zeldovich) is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Repeated by BOSS, eBOSS, WiggleZ, 6dF and DESI with growing precision; interpretation is stable, but recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy keep the cosmological use under active discussion.
uncertainties: Relative importance of the prediction and the detection is unresolved.
Dependence on survey collaborations makes individual credit difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar-timing arrays gave evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, opening a new band in gravitational-wave astronomy through patient timing of millisecond pulsars. This is a long-baseline measurement achievement.
assessment.attribution: The credit should span the three pulsar-timing arrays: McLaughlin for NANOGrav, Kramer for EPTA and Manchester for PPTA. This is a reasonable regional balance, but the decisive contributions were collective, and others such as the founders of the pulsar-timing method may have claims.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 evidence came at roughly 3 to 4 sigma with Hellings-Downs correlation, not yet a firm discovery of source or origin; recognition now would be premature.
uncertainties: Whether the signal arises from supermassive black-hole binaries or new physics is unresolved.
Significance is below the traditional five-sigma threshold and awaits IPTA combination.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provided the architecture for superconducting qubit readout and control and underpins much quantum-computing hardware. Impact is large; the experimental design principles are elegant and instrument-oriented.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf provided the theory proposal and first strong-coupling demonstrations. Their credit is plausible but overlaps with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, and with the Yale group's other members.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed widely across laboratories; but recent recognition of the 2025 prize reduces timeliness, and platform competition leaves it unclear which hardware will endure.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize could weigh against it.
I rely on condensed-matter and quantum-information colleagues for relative standing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's full-sky microwave maps yielded precision cosmological parameters and established the standard cosmological model, building on COBE. It was a major instrument-driven advance.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page led instrument design and the beam and systematic work, and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. It is a plausible trio, though Planck's later higher precision and the ACT/SPT contributions blur attribution.
assessment.maturity: Superseded in precision by Planck but well confirmed; recognition is late and partly overlapped by earlier cosmology awards in 2006 and 2019.
uncertainties: The Planck mission and the 2019 cosmology prize may make this less compelling.
Collaboration leadership versus individual decisive contributions is hard to separate.
